Source. On witness line 4 `[P]S]`, `char_search()` stops at the first `]`, so this passes the one-byte name `P` into `flb_cf_section_create()`. `get_section_type()` therefore classifies the new section as `FLB_CF_PARSER` and links it into `cf->parsers`, making later properties on this section reachable from `parser_conf_file()`.

The first property line under this section causes `indent` to become the one-byte string `"L"` because the loop increments `i` once before testing blanks. When later lines 8 and 9 begin with `Lregex` and `Lformat`, `check_indent()` matches that same prefix and `indent_len = 1` strips the leading `L`, so the effective keys start at `regex` and `format`.

On witness line 8 `Lregex 11 c7 c7 c7 2e 53 2f 2a ec`, step 2 makes `key == "regex"` and `val_len == 9`. `flb_cf_property_add()` duplicates those 9 bytes into `current_section->properties`, so the parser section now carries the exact regex payload that later reaches Onigmo.
When `parser_conf_file()` iterates the parser section from step 1, this retrieves the step-4 property as the SDS string `"regex"`.

This retrieves the step-3 property and sends it through `get_parser_key()` to `flb_env_var_translate()`. For the staged witness, `strlen(value) == 9`, so `flb_sds_create_size(9)` allocates the 26-byte SDS region that the saved ASan allocation stack later identifies as the overread source object.
The step-5 string compares equal to `"regex"`, so the new parser is classified as `FLB_PARSER_REGEX`. This decision is the control precondition for the `flb_regex_create(p_regex)` block.
Because step 7 selected `FLB_PARSER_REGEX`, the line-206 `if (p->type == FLB_PARSER_REGEX)` gate is taken and this call forwards the step-6 SDS as `p_regex` into the regex compiler.

For the staged payload `11 c7 c7 c7 2e 53 2f 2a ec`, `strlen(pattern) == 9`. Because the value neither begins nor ends with `'/'`, `start` stays at `pattern` and `end` becomes `pattern + 9` before `onig_new()` receives the logical UTF-8 span.

At the trailing payload byte `0xec`, UTF-8 precise decode needs two more continuation bytes. This helper therefore turns `NEEDMORE(2)` into `enclen(enc, p, end) == 3`, which is larger than the single byte still available before the logical `end`.

Root cause. `fetch_token()` records the token start and then advances `p += enclen(enc, p, end)` through `PFETCH(c)`. On the crashing token, step 10 supplied `enclen == 3` even though only the final payload byte remained, so `p` moves from the last regex byte to `end + 2`. The vulnerable file does not check `if (p > end)` here; fixed commit `9cc2ff55a146b2b3e8c321a87920c0d39a2b2ba6` adds exactly `if (p > end) return ONIGERR_PREMATURE_END_OF_CHAR_CLASS;` after `PFETCH(c);`.

After step 11, `fetch_token()` publishes the advanced cursor as the token end. The exported `*src` now lies two bytes past the true 9-byte `pattern_end`, while `tok->backp` still points at the final in-bounds byte.

`parse_exp()` trusts the span `[tok->backp, *src)` as valid string data and materializes it immediately with `node_new_str()`. The saved ASan crash stack names this exact call site directly above `parse_branch`.

Sink. `onig_node_str_cat()` computes `addlen = end - s` from the step-13 span and then copies `[s, end)` through `onig_strcpy(..., s, end)`. Because that span extends beyond the 9-byte regex payload inside the 26-byte SDS from step 6, this copy produces the saved `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 3` in `onig_node_str_cat -> parse_exp -> parse_branch`.

Root cause. `fetch_token()` records the token start and then advances `p` by `enclen(enc, p, end)` through `PFETCH(c)` without checking whether the resulting pointer escaped the logical regex end.
Sink. The string-node copy block inside `onig_node_str_cat()` trusts the token span `[s, end)` and copies `end - s` bytes from it into node storage.
For the final-byte token, `fetch_token()` publishes `*src` as an end pointer that already exceeds the logical regex `end`.
`node_new_str()` receives the same out-of-bounds token end as its `end` argument when `parse_exp()` materializes the final token span.
